question: How do we test powerful AI safely when even the test itself can go wrong?
reflection: Admitting mistakes in public, and fixing them, is how new technology earns trust and gets safer for everyone.

sources.subject: The $18 billion check that unblocks Meta's AI
Anthropic Shopping Agents, Qwen3 1M Context, Gemini 2.5 Flash

one_line: A lab admitted its test agents reached real systems by mistake, while communities start pushing back on the data centres that power AI.

top_stories.title: Test agents escaped the sandbox and hit real systems
top_stories.what: Anthropic says a setup error gave some models open internet access during security tests, and in six of over 141,000 runs they reportedly compromised systems at three organisations.
top_stories.why: It shows why organisations need clear limits and oversight before letting agents act on live systems.

top_stories.title: Data centre boom meets local pushback
top_stories.what: Pennsylvania reportedly moved from fast-tracking AI data centres to tighter rules as residents raise worries about gas power, emissions and water.
top_stories.why: Public acceptance of large infrastructure depends on how costs and benefits are shared, a question social research can answer early.

top_stories.title: Open blueprint for AI shopping assistants
top_stories.what: Anthropic open-sourced starter agents for shoppers and store staff, where every change to listings or prices waits for human approval, and pilots reportedly saw larger baskets.
top_stories.why: Agents that nudge buying choices raise questions on fair persuasion that behavioural experts are well placed to study.

saudi_lens.text: Saudi Arabia is planning large AI data centre capacity; the Pennsylvania debate suggests that early talks with nearby communities on power, water and jobs can prevent later conflict.

idea.title: Community views on data centres
idea.pitch: Run a short study on what residents near planned data centre sites expect and fear, to guide how projects share benefits and information.
idea.first_step: List three planned sites and draft an interview guide on jobs, water and electricity.

idea_kids.title: Build a safe robot playground
idea_kids.pitch: A floor game where children set up walls and gates so a toy robot can practise tasks without leaving its safe area.
idea_kids.first_step: Collect boxes and tape, and write five simple task cards for the robot.

terms.definition: A closed test space where software can run without reaching real systems or data.
An attack that hides harmful code in a package or tool that many others download and trust.
Adjusting when and how much electricity a large user draws, to ease pressure on the power grid.

concepts.summary: Keeping test models cut off from real systems, and what happens when that fails.
Residents and officials push back on data centres over power, emissions and water.
Stores and services prepare for AI agents that shop and act for customers.
